PullRequest.Title: agentHost: review notebook edits in the editor with Keep and Undo
PullRequest.Body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.

-->

Agent Host sessions edit notebooks as files on disk, and the editor review skipped notebooks. Their changes showed no diff in the notebook editor and could only be kept or undone as a whole from the working set. This reviews them in the notebook editor like local chat edits.

### What changed and why

- **Notebooks are reviewed by their cells.** `AgentHostEditReview` now creates an entry for a notebook, built on the local chat notebook entry, that compares the open notebook with the notebook in the Working Set file's baseline. The host still owns what is kept: Keep and Undo invoke its Accept Changes and Discard Changes operations.
- **The change of one cell can be kept or undone on its own, for ipynb files.** The host decides on a file or on a range of its lines, so the new `agentHostNotebookFileChanges.ts` locates a cell's change in the lines of the ipynb file. The host acts on whole hunks of its line diff, and a hunk isn't always one cell's change: cells added one after the other are a single hunk. The range is therefore only sent when keeping or undoing the hunks it selects yields exactly that change; otherwise the action reports that the file has to be decided as a whole. Other notebook types and newly created notebooks are decided as a whole.
- **Unsaved changes of a notebook are told apart.** The ipynb extension gives the cells of a loaded notebook ids, which leaves the notebook with unsaved changes and keeps it from reloading what the agent writes next. Unsaved changes that are only those are dropped so the review can follow the agent. Any other unsaved change counts as the user's: it is never dropped, and it suspends the review until the notebook is saved or reverted.
- **Changes saved outside of the session aren't shown as the agent's.** When the file differs from what the session recorded, those changes are folded into the notebook that the review compares with. Such a notebook is decided as a whole, since its lines are no longer the recorded ones.
- **A notebook follows an Undo from the working set.** The working set above the chat input invokes the host directly. A notebook whose only unsaved changes are generated ids doesn't reload the reverted file by itself, so the review loads it when the file leaves the Working Set.
- **The Keep/Undo overlay shows for notebook editors.** `ChatEditingOverlayController` only handled panes with a code editor (#312332), so the overlay never appeared for a notebook. Notebook panes are handled now, and an entry only matches the kind of editor that reviews it. This code is shared with local chat.
- **The shared notebook review code has hooks for a host-owned review.** `canDecideCells` and `IDocumentDiff2.decidedTogether` hide the per-hunk and per-cell actions when cells can't be decided one by one. `ICellDiffInfo.keepAll` and `undoAll` let the Markdown preview toolbar decide all hunks of a cell in one operation, because each host operation replaces the remaining hunks. `ChatEditingModifiedNotebookEntry` exposes how its comparison notebook is resolved and replaced, and whether it settles once no changes are left. The defaults keep the behavior of local chat.
- **The inline hunk toolbar stays inside short editors.** It is taller than a line, so the editor of a one-line notebook cell cut it off. It now moves up where the editor can't scroll further.
- **Tests** cover the review of notebooks, the location of cell changes in ipynb files, and the toolbar position. The chat contribution tests build the review as well, so their setup now provides the notebook services it uses.

This branch also has an earlier commit that removes two doc comments in `chatProgressContentPart.ts`, which isn't part of this change.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The new compare call runs after each changed Working Set version. The traced superclass rebuild disposes cell entries without removing them from its lifetime DisposableStore, and creates uniquely named empty text models owned by that same store. DisposableStore retains explicitly disposed children until the parent is cleared. No profiling is required to establish retention; its practical size depends on notebook size and update count.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Obsolete ChatEditingNotebookCellEntry objects and their referenced cell/model state, plus live emptyCell ITextModel instances
Findings.PerformanceScaling: For V comparison rebuilds and C paired/inserted cells, retained entry objects grow approximately O(V*C); empty models grow with the sum of inserted/deleted cells across all rebuilds, rather than only the current diff size.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Increasing retained memory and GC pressure over the lifetime of an agent-host notebook review
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Agent-host notebook edits were skipped by editor review, so repeated host writes did not create or retain notebook comparison generations.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Each host notebook version rebuilds all cell diff entries in a long-lived notebook entry, but the inherited ownership retains resources from obsolete generations until the entire file review ends.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The added AgentHostNotebookReviewEntry.compare invokes initializeModelsFromDiff at line 444 on every _followNotebook update. Previously _createEntry returned immediately for supported notebooks and allocated none of these resources.
Findings.Title: Release the previous comparison's cell resources before rebuilding
Findings.Impact: During a multi-step agent edit of a notebook with hundreds of cells, each published version retains another set of obsolete cell-entry objects; persistent inserted/deleted cells also accumulate live empty text models. Memory grows throughout the undecided review and increases GC pressure even though only the latest comparison is displayed.
Findings.Evidence: _followNotebook calls entry.compare after deserializing each new version. ChatEditingModifiedNotebookEntry.initializeModelsFromDiffImpl (219-235) disposes and clears cellEntryMap, but getOrCreateModifiedTextFileEntryForCell (1064) registers every new entry in the parent _store. Disposing those children does not remove them from DisposableStore._toDispose. Each retained ChatEditingNotebookCellEntry still references its cell and original/modified models. createInsertedCellDiffInfo (771-772) and createDeleteCellDiffInfo (814-815) additionally create a unique NewModelCounter-based emptyCell text model and register it for the whole notebook lifetime, with no generation cleanup.
Findings.Recommendation: Give rebuilt comparison resources a disposable generation owner and clear it before replacing the diff. Remove disposed cell entries from the lifetime store, release obsolete empty models and cell references, and evict obsolete cache entries while preserving models needed by the current comparison.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The action-to-locate-to-computeHunks call chain is synchronous in browser code. The default diff implementation hashes every line and performs line/character diffing, and the helper reparses whole reconstructed notebooks. The 500 ms limit applies to diff computation, not to the surrounding parsing. Exact pause duration varies with notebook size and changes; the UI-blocking mechanism is directly established.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Renderer-thread CPU work and allocations for full-file JSON parsing, line/character diffing, candidate reconstruction, and content comparison
Findings.PerformanceScaling: One full-file diff and four full notebook parses per cell/hunk decision that reaches validation; cost grows with total notebook file bytes/lines, including outputs, and repeats with the number of decisions. A cell-wide toolbar coalesces its hunks into one operation, not one operation per source line.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Blocked UI critical path and delayed Keep/Undo response, with dropped frames during large notebook validation
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Agent-host notebooks could only be decided as whole files; no renderer-side full-file diff or reconstructed-notebook validation ran for those decisions. Existing text range mapping uses the asynchronous IEditorWorkerService diff path.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: A cell/hunk Keep or Undo now synchronously parses both full ipynb versions, diffs their complete file lines, reconstructs and parses two full candidate notebooks, and compares their contents before issuing the host operation.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The new computeHunks directly calls linesDiffComputers.getDefault().computeDiff on both complete notebook files with a 500 ms budget. The new notebook range operation invokes this synchronously through entry.locate before invokeChangesetOperation.
Findings.Title: Move full-notebook hunk validation off the UI thread
Findings.Impact: Keeping or undoing one cell in a large output-bearing ipynb blocks workbench input and rendering while processing the entire notebook, even if that cell has a small source change. Difficult diffs can consume the configured 500 ms computation budget, in addition to unbounded-by-that-budget parsing/copying, and repeat on each decision.
Findings.Evidence: AgentHostEditReview._invokeOperation calls entry.locate(change) at 1397. AgentHostNotebookReviewEntry.locate (366-378) calls readNotebookFile twice and locateNotebookFileChange. That helper calls computeHunks (162), whose new line 270 runs the default line diff inline; lines 171-174 copy/join and parse two full notebooks and compare all expected cells. DefaultLinesDiffComputer maps/hashes all original and modified lines and refines character differences. All of this executes without yielding before the host RPC, and there is no cached validation for the immutable version pair.
Findings.Recommendation: Run the version-pair diff and candidate validation in a worker, preserving the exact host hunk-selection rules and timeout handling. Revalidate the Working Set version and cell change after awaiting the result; the existing editor worker service already provides asynchronous advanced diff operations.

Scenarios.Scenario: Enable or resume agent-host review with notebook files in the Working Set, including notebooks not open in an editor
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The _updates sequencer awaits _update, which visits files serially. Notebook model resolution, serializer availability, _followNotebook and the notebook-level diff must finish before subsequent files and queued decisions progress. Per-cell diff promises can finish afterward.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read immutable baseline and current snapshot through connection.resourceRead, decoding base64 response bytes
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Two snapshot reads per non-created changed file; one for a created file. Provider concurrency is capped at 10, normally only the current pair is issued by this review.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same _readContents call preceded the old notebook skip, so these snapshot reads already occurred.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Both reads must finish before entry creation or update.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve the actual notebook working copy, reading its on-disk file if not already resolved
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One cold working-copy file load per notebook; warm model references avoid a new initial load.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Editor review skipped the notebook and did not resolve its working copy.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited before creating the notebook entry.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Serialize notebook bytes across the extension-host boundary and deserialize them into cell/output DTOs
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Normally four deserializations on cold creation: the actual file, the comparison file, then baseline/current in _followNotebook. With an already-resolved actual model, normally three. Reloading a divergent actual file adds one. Provider activation occurs once per cold view type, not per cell.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No notebook serializer requests were issued by agent-host editor review.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Notebook resolution and the baseline/current pair are awaited on the serial update path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Synchronize notebook cell/source/output DTOs to the notebook worker and compute notebook alignment; subsequently request text diffs for cell pairs
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Two notebook models synchronized once per entry, then incremental events. Constructor and initial compare can each issue a notebook diff, with stale results discarded. Each completed rebuild creates cell entries for all paired and inserted cells, which request their own editor-worker text diffs.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No notebook or cell comparison workers were reached by this review.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Notebook alignment is awaited; cell text diff requests are not awaited by initializeModelsFromDiffImpl.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: N changed notebook resources, C cells per notebook, and total serialized notebook bytes including outputs; resources are handled once per file version, not per cell.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Files are serial within one review and all updates use its sequencer. Baseline/current snapshot reads run as a pair. Host filesystem resourceRead has a provider-wide limiter of 10. Each _followNotebook issues two serializer calls concurrently; extension-host synchronous parsing still runs on that host's event loop. Cell model resolutions and per-cell diff requests fan out; each cell change service coalesces/sequences only its own requests, not the whole notebook.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Same original URI, modified snapshot URI, creation status and nonce skip an existing non-editing entry. Cold modified notebook resolution reads and deserializes its file; warm references reuse the model. Snapshot content reads have no provider data cache. Serializer activation is shared per view type; the comparison file provider stores one buffer per entry and removes it on disposal.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the serial update loop, new notebook-resolution branch, serializer IPC, worker synchronization and cache checks are directly traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Notebook sizes, output volumes and cold serializer activation duration are not measured. Large unopened Working Sets increase latency, but no separate speculative eager-loading finding is submitted.
Scenarios.Verdict: The feature introduces notebook review work on the serial update path. The concrete resource-lifetime regression is reported separately; inherent feature initialization costs are not independently reported.

Scenarios.Scenario: Follow successive agent writes or refreshed notebook versions while changes remain undecided
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A new snapshot URI or nonce triggers _readContents and _followNotebook. Deserialization, content equality, optional file reload, comparison snapshot replacement and notebook diff must finish before the update sequencer advances.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read the version's baseline and current recorded file contents
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Two reads per processed existing-file version, one for created notebooks, independent of cell count.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Snapshot contents were already read before notebook review was skipped.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Deserialize the complete recorded baseline and current notebook in the extension host
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Two full-file serializer calls per processed version, even when the baseline content is unchanged.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No follow/deserialization pipeline existed for notebook review.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Force-read or revert the actual notebook working copy when it does not hold the recorded current content
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Zero if the file watcher already brought the model up to date; otherwise one forced file load and associated serializer call per follow attempt.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Editor review did not force notebook reloads; normal notebook file-watcher behavior was independent.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited before comparing; user-unsaved changes suspend review instead.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Compute notebook alignment and rebuild cell-level comparison entries and worker diffs
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One notebook diff per compare when models differ; all paired/inserted cells are rebuilt, not just changed cells. Identical notebooks bypass notebook-worker alignment but still rebuild the cell entries.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Notebook versions allocated no editor-review comparison generations.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Notebook alignment is awaited; cell diffs continue asynchronously.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: V published versions, C current cell pairs, I inserted cells and D deleted cells per version, plus full notebook bytes. Unrelated unchanged files with identical version keys are skipped.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Notebook versions are processed serially per review. Two serializer requests run as a pair. Notebook diffs are awaited; per-cell text diffs are launched independently, with sequencing/coalescing only within each cell service. Cancellation discards superseded updates but does not cancel serializer work already issued.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Existing notebook models and successfully resolved cell text models are reused by URI. The version key prevents same-version reprocessing except when finishing agent editing. Baseline/current DTOs are deserialized anew for every processed version. Empty comparison models get a new counter-based URI on every rebuild, so they cannot hit a previous cache entry.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: Very high: compare unconditionally rebuilds, inherited creation registers resources in the lifetime store, and inherited rebuild only disposes/clears cellEntryMap without removing old registrations.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The number of agent writes before a decision and the largest notebook cell count are unknown; retained-object multiplicity is established independently of those prevalence uncertainties.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reported unbounded-retention regression: obsolete cell-entry objects remain in the lifetime store and inserted/deleted cells accumulate live uniquely named empty models across versions.

Scenarios.Scenario: Keep or Undo one ipynb cell or source hunk
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The global-per-review operation sequencer first waits for pending updates and Working Set readiness, then synchronously locates/validates the notebook file range before issuing the host operation. Updated Working Set review is awaited afterward.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Parse both full ipynb versions, synchronously diff all file lines, reconstruct/parse two complete candidate notebooks and compare expected cells
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One full line diff and four full parses per decision that reaches candidate validation. Parsing is not bounded by the diff's 500 ms timeout.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Notebooks had whole-file decisions only, with no renderer-side notebook hunk validation; existing text range mapping used asynchronous editor-worker diffing.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks renderer input/rendering and precedes issuance of the host operation.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Invoke the host Accept/Discard Changes operation with a validated file-line range and version nonce
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One RPC for a successful cell/hunk decision; none for unmatched/inseparable changes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: This cell-range operation did not exist for notebooks; whole-resource host Keep/Undo was already supported elsewhere.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited, then followed by the host's ready update and review refresh.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Total file bytes and lines, including large outputs, and number of user decisions. One selected source hunk or cell is validated per operation. The Markdown cell toolbar coalesces all that cell's hunks into one host operation.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Exactly one decision executes at a time per review. Validation is synchronous on the renderer thread, not worker work. There is one host operation per successful decision, not per cell source line or per hunk within keepAll/undoAll.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Entry source models and recorded strings are available, but parsed notebook file structures, complete line diff and kept/undone candidates are not cached. Every decision repeats validation for its current version pair.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: Very high: the synchronous action-to-locate-to-computeDiff call chain and all full-file reconstruction/parsing operations are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: No timing measurements; pauses depend on full notebook size, output payload and diff difficulty. The 500 ms budget is a configured computation bound, not an asserted measured pause.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reported synchronous-ui-work regression. Required exact hunk validation should remain semantically intact but run off the renderer thread with post-await version checks.

Scenarios.Scenario: Keep/Undo a whole notebook, including generated cell IDs, user-unsaved changes and decisions made from the Working Set outside the editor
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Editor operations wait on the operation/update sequencers. Undo may await saving genuine user changes, then the host operation, then a generated-dirty notebook reload. For externally decided notebooks, _update awaits generated-dirty file inspection/reload before removing the entry.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Save genuine user-unsaved notebook changes before Undo, or reload the reverted file without saving generated-only changes
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one preparatory user save or temporary generated-dirty reference acquisition per Undo, followed by a conditional reload if still generated-dirty. Saving/reloading invokes the authoritative serializer.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Editor review skipped notebooks; Working Set whole-file host decisions did not perform these notebook working-copy steps.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited before/after the host decision to preserve user edits and prevent restoring undone content.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Invoke Accept/Discard Changes for one notebook resource
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One host operation per notebook, regardless of cells/hunks.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Whole-resource operations already existed from the Working Set; the notebook editor now reaches the same host boundary.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited before observing the ready Working Set and finishing the decision.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read a notebook that left the Working Set, deserialize it and conditionally revert/reload its generated-dirty model
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One inspection read and serializer call per generated-only dirty removed notebook; zero for clean or genuinely user-dirty notebooks. A differing model adds one working-copy reload and serializer call.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No notebook-entry removal hook existed; normal file watching was the only reload mechanism.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: On the serial update/removal path; required to avoid generated-dirty models later saving reverted agent content back.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of decided notebook resources, full file size and whether each notebook is dirty due to generated IDs or user changes; clean/user-dirty removals are skipped by _loadDecidedNotebook.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Editor decisions are serialized per review even if accept/reject initially uses Promise.all. Removed notebooks are inspected serially in _update. No per-cell host RPC fan-out is added for whole-file decisions.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Generated-change state is tracked per URI and cleared on clean/removal events. Notebook references are reused; a temporary Undo reference is released in finally. Comparison buffer registration is released with entry disposal, except an open diff editor intentionally retains the entry until that editor closes.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: guards, authoritative notebook save/reload paths, host operation cardinality and finally-based reference cleanup are traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Remote filesystem latency and the fraction of generated-dirty notebooks are not measured; reload duplication depends on dirty-event ordering and is not asserted as a separate issue.
Scenarios.Verdict: No separate high-confidence regression beyond retained comparison generations. New I/O placement implements required synchronization and is guarded by dirty/content checks.

Scenarios.Scenario: Follow externally saved notebook edits or suspend review while the user has unsaved edits
Scenarios.CriticalPath: When the recorded current notebook differs from the live model, _followNotebook checks user changes, reloads if allowed, and if divergence remains computes an adjusted baseline before comparing. Genuine user-unsaved divergence suspends review until a save/revert dirty event retries it.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Deserialize the baseline/current pair through the notebook serializer
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Two calls per processed version before suspension/outside-change detection.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Agent-host review did not inspect notebooks.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Reload actual notebook contents to distinguish delayed file watching from outside-session saves
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One conditional working-copy reload per divergent follow attempt; skipped for genuine user-unsaved changes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Only the normal notebook working-copy watcher followed these files.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited before determining the adjusted comparison baseline.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Snapshot current cell data, compare cell-source sequences and restore/serialize an adjusted comparison notebook
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Two LCS calculations only when live sources differ from recorded current; one comparison snapshot serialization per successful compare.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No outside-notebook baseline adjustment existed in editor review.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Cell count and source bytes of baseline/current/live notebooks; outside-change adjustment computes two cell sequence diffs, not a network request per cell.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Runs on the serial update path. Baseline/current serializer calls are a pair; withOutsideChanges performs two synchronous LcsDiff calculations. No additional process or network fan-out comes from the cell loops.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Same-version entries normally skip updates; changed versions repeat deserialization. Generated-only classification is not a saved-content cache. Outside-adjusted baselines disable independent cell decisions so obsolete recorded line ranges are not reused.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for call path and conditional multiplicity; exact duration is unknown.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: LCS costs depend on cell count and edit distance; no realistic independently severe outside-change case was established beyond the reported generation retention.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional finding. The user-change safeguards and baseline adjustments are intentional semantics; comparison-generation retention is already reported.

Scenarios.Scenario: Track notebook dirty metadata across sessions and display shared Keep/Undo overlays and inline toolbars during input, layout and scrolling
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Each enabled review installs notebook event listeners and classifies generated metadata in a microtask. Visible editor overlays react through observables. Hunk widget layout runs synchronously on layout/scroll and on toolbar visibility changes.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read computed margins and widget dimensions while positioning each hunk overlay
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One new height measurement per widget layout; the pre-existing width measurement already reads computed margins and offsetWidth on the same path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Each widget layout already measured width and updated its overlay position; the diff adds a height clamp for short notebook cell editors.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Synchronous in scroll/layout handling, but no independently introduced extra forced-layout cycle is established.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Enabled reviews S, open notebooks and their cell counts; metadata events are processed per raw event. Structural cell changes rescan a notebook's cells. Hunk layouts scale with rendered hunk widgets in the active editor, including local chat.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Event and DOM work run on the renderer thread. Metadata classification is microtask-coalesced per tracker. No subprocess/filesystem/database/network operation is triggered by the new overlay matching or height measurement.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Metadata references are weakly keyed by cell; notebook listener disposables and URI state are removed when notebooks close. _recent coalesces dirty/content classification within a microtask. Toolbar pooling and delayed hiding are retained; the new decidedTogether flag suppresses unsupported per-hunk toolbars.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for listener ownership, coalescing and existing/new geometry reads; insufficient evidence for an independent layout regression.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The number of concurrent review trackers, metadata size and active hunk count vary. No evidence establishes an additional forced layout beyond the existing width read.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional high-confidence issue. Event cleanup is owned, weak metadata references do not pin removed cells, and the new height read alone does not prove materially amplified layout thrashing. Progress-message changes remove comments only.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the distinct performance-review pass across all 13 changed files and all diff pages, tracing notebook resolution, serializer/worker IPC, host filesystem limits, decision sequencing, dirty-state ownership and shared UI layout. Submitted two high-confidence introduced regressions: retained obsolete comparison generations and renderer-thread full-notebook cell-decision validation. No concrete regression fix with blame-worthy provenance was identified. Review was static; magnitude is unmeasured.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
